{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Continuous positive-valued outcome with wide range (0.5-201.4s) suggests right skew; consider log transformation or robust ANOVA if diagnostics fail.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73 violates normality assumption for standard ANOVA. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or generalized linear model with binomial family and logit link. Report odds ratios relative to Sham baseline.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Range spans 0.0009 to 29.8 with mean 0.47, indicating extreme right skew and potential outliers. Log transformation or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test recommended as primary analysis.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Range 0.12-75.35 cm/s with moderate positive skew; assess normality of residuals and consider transformation if needed.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38; beta regression or arcsine-square-root transformation appropriate given bounded nature, though standard ANOVA may suffice if diagnostics pass."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed from experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice using autocorrelation function on residuals.",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals for each continuous outcome; severe departures expected for Path Efficiency and Success.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances across Stim Paradigm groups; unequal sample sizes (n=3,505 to 48,846) reduce robustness to variance heterogeneity.",
    "Outliers: Visual inspection of boxplots and Cook's distance; Path Efficiency shows extreme max value (29.8) requiring investigation.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined group dominates (63.7% of data), reducing power for pairwise comparisons involving smaller groups like Sham (4.6%) and Bright Visual Only (4.3%)."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous outcomes meeting ANOVA assumptions: Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons with family-wise error rate control, accounting for unequal sample sizes via Tukey-Kramer adjustment.",
    "For outcomes requiring non-parametric approach (Path Efficiency, potentially AD): Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons.",
    "For binary Success outcome: Pairwise logistic regression contrasts with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment, or marginal means from emmeans package with multiplicity correction.",
    "Planned contrasts: Sham vs. active stimulation conditions (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) to assess stimulation benefit; unisensory (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) vs. Combined to test multisensory enhancement.",
    "Effect sizes: Report eta-squared or partial eta-squared for ANOVA; Cohen's d for pairwise comparisons; odds ratios for Success model."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham group shows markedly worse performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236), suggesting stimulation generally improves navigation.",
    "Combined stimulation appears superior to unisensory conditions: highest Success (0.780), fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), highest Path Efficiency (0.502), highest Average Speed (12.83), and highest AD (0.399), consistent with multisensory integration benefits.",
    "Visual stimulation alone shows modality-dependent effects: Bright Visual Only outperforms Dim Visual Only on Success (0.785 vs 0.673), Time-to-Target (2.61 vs 3.14s), Path Efficiency (0.504 vs 0.434), and AD (0.387 vs 0.336), suggesting luminance matters for visual guidance.",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only show similar intermediate performance: Success ~0.68-0.69, Time-to-Target ~3.05-3.14s, Path Efficiency ~0.43, suggesting comparable efficacy of intracortical microstimulation and dim visual cues.",
    "AD pattern (Sham < Dim Visual < ICMS Only < Bright Visual < Combined) suggests stimulation enhances directional stability, with multisensory and brighter visual conditions producing straighter paths."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Massive sample size imbalance: Combined group (n=48,846) dwarfs Sham (n=3,505) and Bright Visual Only (n=3,323), causing ANOVA to be dominated by Combined group variance and reducing precision for small-group comparisons.",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored: 8 mice contribute multiple trials; failure to account for within-mouse correlation inflates Type I error rates and violates independence assumption.",
    "No covariate adjustment: Mouse identity, learning effects over time, and trial-specific factors (e.g., target location, distance) not controlled, potentially confounding paradigm effects.",
    "Binary Success treated as continuous in summary statistics; proper analysis requires generalized linear model, not standard ANOVA.",
    "Path Efficiency extreme values (max 29.8, mean 0.47) indicate calculation anomalies or data quality issues requiring investigation before inference.",
    "Cross-sectional comparison only: No within-mouse crossover design to control for individual differences in baseline ability."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) for Success, with random intercepts for Mouse and fixed effects for Stim Paradigm. This addresses the repeated measures structure, accounts for within-mouse correlation, and permits more reliable inference despite sample size imbalance. For Path Efficiency, use robust regression or examine data quality for extreme values. Include trial number or session as covariate to assess learning effects. If computational constraints prevent mixed models, use clustered standard errors or aggregate to mouse-level means with weighted ANOVA."
}
